title: Analyses manifest
description: One row per analysis. An analysis is a comparison/finding OVER CONDITIONS (studies compare conditions, so the target is conditions_compared, not runs). This is where study findings live, and where preregistration linkage is recorded ('we did what we said, modulo errata'). Hybrid: the generator machine-fills analysis_id, output_path, working_notes_obs; humans author outcome, paper_section, and the prereg linkage. The generator never overwrites human-authored fields.

analysis_id.description: Primary key. Convention: the results/ subdir name (lowercased, hyphenated). For a top-level .md analysis, the filename stem.

conditions_compared.description: Foreign keys to condition_id. CHANGED from the brief's runs_compared — studies compare conditions; the run/study are derivable from the conditions.

hypothesis_refs.description: HUMAN-authored. Controlled vocabulary: H1..H15 plus documented named programmes.

deviations.description: HUMAN-authored. D-/E-numbers from decisions-log.md / protocol-errata.md (the 'modulo errata and amendments' demonstration).

predicted_outcome.description: HUMAN-authored. What the preregistration predicted, for the predicted-vs-actual comparison. WRITE-ONCE: once non-null, the generator refuses to overwrite it (a prediction is only evidence of foresight if it cannot be edited once the result is known). To change it legitimately, add predicted_outcome_amended.

predicted_outcome_amended.description: HUMAN-authored. The declared, auditable escape hatch from the write-once rule on predicted_outcome. Its presence permits the rewrite AND records it in the manifest, so an amended prediction is visibly amended rather than silently restated.

reason.description: Why the prediction changed. A result being known is NOT a reason.

date.description: ISO-8601 date on which the amendment was made.

previous.description: The EXACT superseded prediction as it stands on disk. Required, and checked: an amendment whose previous does not match the on-disk value is rejected, so an amendment supersedes one specific prediction rather than unlocking the field permanently.

tie_set.description: HUMAN-authored. Conditions found statistically indistinguishable (from a permutation/CI-overlap test). This is where a statistical tie is recorded — NOT by hard-coding a 'best' condition on the run.

output_path.description: results/<analysis_id>/ for a subdir analysis, or the path to a top-level .md file.

manually_verified_at.description: Set when a human authors/verifies the row. The generator treats a non-null value as a signal not to overwrite the human-authored fields.

analysis.$comment: Lenient back-fill policy: the machine-fillable fields (analysis_id, type, conditions_compared, output_path, provenance) are required; all human-authored fields are nullable so a generator-created stub validates before a human authors it.
